mainTopic: Partnerships in wine and oil for a שיתוף: connection of liquids, ברירה, and relying on a שיתוף in place of an עירוב
overview: רב יוסף explains the משנה's dispute about a partnership in wine and oil. He says it is the same argument as the one between רבי יוחנן בן נורי and the רבנן: whether oil floating on wine counts as connected to it. Next, a ברייתא brings רבי אליעזר בן תדאי, who requires an עירוב even when both partners share wine. רבה explains that everyone agrees wine poured from each partner's jug into one barrel works. The argument is only about a barrel bought together, and it depends on ברירה. רב יוסף instead says the argument is whether we may rely on a שיתוף in place of an עירוב. He proves this from רב, who ruled like both רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר בן תדאי. אביי asks why רב needed two rulings, and the answer is that in עירובין we do not take on two stringencies automatically. The גמרא then quotes the ברייתא of רבי מאיר and the חכמים, and רבי נחומי and רבה begin to argue about when that dispute applies. The second opinion comes on the next amud.

steps.title: רב יוסף links the dispute to a different known argument
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that רבי שמעון and the רבנן are arguing about the same issue that רבי יוחנן בן נורי and the רבנן argue about elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: רבי שמעון and the רבנן are disagreeing about the same point that רבי יוחנן בן נורי and the רבנן disagree about.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a new explanation of why רבי שמעון and the רבנן argue in our משנה. He sets up a comparison to another famous dispute, and the גמרא will quote that source next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier explanation placed the argument in a different setup. רב יוסף says the setup is a single alley, so the whole question is about the wine and oil themselves. In his view, the issue is whether two different liquids sitting together count as one connected unit.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis
phrases.notes: The two sides of the dispute in our משנה about a partnership in wine and oil.

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי וְרַבָּנַן
phrases.english: in the dispute of Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri and the Rabbis
are disagreeing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation of the משנה's dispute, different from the explanation given on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between רבי שמעון and the רבנן is the same as the argument between רבי יוחנן בן נורי and the רבנן.

steps.title: The source: oil floating on wine touched by a טבול יום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about oil floating on wine. The רבנן say only the oil becomes פסול. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says the oil and wine are connected.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If oil was floating on top of wine, and a טבול יום touched the oil, he made only the oil פסול. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: the two are connected to each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the other dispute that רב יוסף is pointing to. This is the background source his comparison is built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טבול יום who touches תרומה makes it פסול. The question is whether the wine underneath also becomes פסול. The רבנן treat the oil and wine as two separate things. רבי יוחנן בן נורי treats them as one connected unit (חיבור), so the wine is also פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: someone who immersed today but must wait until nightfall to be fully טהור

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is about טומאה, not about עירוב. The גמרא brings it only for one idea: whether two different liquids touching each other count as one connected thing.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
Oil that floats on top of wine,
phrases.notes: This refers to oil of תרומה.

phrases.english: and a tevul yom touched the oil —
he disqualified only the oil alone,
phrases.notes: The wine stays fit, because it is considered separate from the oil.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says:
the two of them are connected to each other.
phrases.notes: So the wine is also disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source text that רב יוסף's comparison relies on.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that our dispute matches the dispute of רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about oil floating on wine touched by a טבול יום.

steps.title: Matching each side to its parallel
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן of our משנה agree with the רבנן there. רבי שמעון agrees with רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן here hold like the רבנן there, and רבי שמעון holds like רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב יוסף's comparison by matching up the opinions. The רבנן say wine and oil are separate, and רבי שמעון says they are connected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wine and oil are separate, a partnership in wine and oil is not one shared food, so it cannot work as an עירוב. That is the view of the רבנן. If they are connected, the wine and oil count as one shared item, so the partnership does work. That is why רבי שמעון says no separate עירוב is needed.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף, the whole argument about a wine-and-oil partnership comes down to one question: are wine and oil one connected unit (רבי שמעון) or two separate things (the רבנן)?

phrases.english: The Rabbis — are like the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: Wine and oil are separate, so the partnership is not an עירוב.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן — כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon — is like Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.
phrases.notes: Wine and oil are connected, so the partnership works as an עירוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן כְּרַבָּנַן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the quoted source to the two opinions in our משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The רבנן hold that wine and oil are separate, so the partnership is not an עירוב. רבי שמעון holds that they are connected, so the partnership counts.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן תדאי: both cases need an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי אליעזר בן תדאי, who says that in both cases, wine-and-wine and wine-and-oil, they must still make an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר בן תדאי says: in both this case and that case, they must make an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, stricter opinion. רבי אליעזר בן תדאי says that in both cases, wine-with-wine and wine-with-oil, the partners still need to make an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said that a partnership in wine alone is enough. רבי אליעזר בן תדאי disagrees and requires an עירוב even then. This opens a new line of discussion.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Taddai says:
both this one and that one
phrases.notes: The wine-and-wine case and the wine-and-oil case.

phrases.english: need to make an eiruv.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן תַּדַּאי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a third opinion, stricter than both sides of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a partnership in wine alone requires a separate עירוב.

steps.title: Surprise: even wine with wine?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised. Does רבי אליעזר בן תדאי really require an עירוב even when both partners share wine?
steps.simpleTranslation: And even when this one is in wine and that one is in wine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expresses surprise at רבי אליעזר בן תדאי's ruling. This question sets up רבה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine shared with wine is clearly the same kind of item. So why shouldn't it count as one combined food for an עירוב? The question shows that his opinion seems too strict to make sense.

phrases.english: And even with this one in wine
and with that one in wine?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how far רבי אליעזר בן תדאי's ruling extends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי אליעזר בן תדאי really say that a wine-with-wine partnership needs an עירוב? It seems that it should obviously count.

steps.title: רבה: if both poured into one container, everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that if each partner poured his own jug into the same container, everyone agrees it counts as an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: If this one came with his jug and poured, and that one came with his jug and poured, everyone agrees that it is an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the surprise by limiting רבי אליעזר בן תדאי's ruling. When the wine was actually mixed together in one container, even he agrees it works as an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring the wine together turns it into one real shared mixture. So in that case nobody argues. רבי אליעזר בן תדאי's strict ruling must therefore be about a different kind of partnership, where the wine was not actually combined this way.

keyTerms.meaning: everyone agrees, there is no dispute
the shared food that joins the residents' properties so they may carry on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: When both partners poured their wine into the same container, everyone agrees it is a valid עירוב, even רבי אליעזר בן תדאי.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
If this one came with his jug and poured,
phrases.notes: He poured it into a shared barrel.

phrases.english: and that one came with his jug and poured —
everyone agrees
that it is an eiruv.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה זֶה בָּא בִּלְגִינוֹ וְשָׁפַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the surprise of step 5 by identifying a case where everyone agrees.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When both partners poured their wine into the same container, it is an עירוב according to everyone. So רבי אליעזר בן תדאי's ruling must refer to a different kind of partnership.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the dispute
steps.terutzMaskana: Wine that was actually poured together into one container is a valid עירוב according to all opinions.

steps.title: Where they really argue: a barrel bought together
steps.stepSummary: רבה finishes his answer. The argument is only about partners who bought one barrel of wine together. רבי אליעזר בן תדאי holds אין ברירה, and the רבנן hold יש ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they argue is a case where the partners bought a barrel of wine together. רבי אליעזר בן תדאי holds there is no ברירה. The רבנן hold there is ברירה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה finishes his answer by pointing to the one case where the two sides really disagree: wine the partners bought together as one barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When each partner pours in his own jug, each one clearly owns his part, so everyone agrees it works. When they bought the barrel together, no one owns a specific part until later. If יש ברירה, we can say afterward that each one's share was always his, so it works as an עירוב. If אין ברירה, we cannot say that, so it does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: a later choice that shows which part always belonged to whom

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אליעזר בן תדאי disagrees when each partner poured his own jug. רבה just said everyone agrees about that case. The argument is only about a barrel they bought together.
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the עירוב question to ברירה, a big idea that comes up all over ש"ס.

phrases.english: Where they argue is, for example,
where they bought a barrel of wine in partnership.
Rabbi Eliezer ben Taddai holds:
there is no retroactive clarification,
phrases.notes: We cannot say afterward which part always belonged to each partner.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold: there is retroactive clarification.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי כְּגוֹן שֶׁלָּקְחוּ חָבִית שֶׁל יַיִן בְּשׁוּתָּפוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This finishes רבה's answer. Step 6 gave the case everyone agrees on, and this step gives the case they argue about.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument is only about a jointly bought barrel, and it depends on ברירה.

steps.title: רב יוסף's different explanation of the argument
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the argument is about something else. The question is whether we can rely on a שיתוף instead of an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רבי אליעזר בן תדאי and the רבנן argue about whether we can rely on a שיתוף in place of an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a second, completely different answer to the question from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of ברירה, רב יוסף says the wine here was set up as a שיתוף for the alley. The question is whether that same שיתוף also counts for carrying between the courtyards. On this view, רבי אליעזר בן תדאי requires a separate עירוב because he does not allow the שיתוף to stand in for it.

keyTerms.meaning: merging of an alley (שיתוף מבואות), which allows carrying in the alley
in place of an עירוב (the one that joins courtyards)

steps.confusionAlert: A שיתוף and an עירוב are two different things. A שיתוף is for the alley, and an עירוב is for the courtyards. The question is whether one can do the job of the other.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Taddai and the Rabbis
about whether one relies on a merging of the alley
in place of an eiruv, they disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This offers a different answer than רבה gave in steps 6 and 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument is about relying on a שיתוף in place of an עירוב, not about ברירה.

steps.title: Spelling out each side according to רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: One side, רבי אליעזר בן תדאי, says we cannot rely on the שיתוף. The other side, the רבנן, says we can.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds we do not rely on it, and the other master holds we do rely on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly who holds what in רב יוסף's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן תדאי says the courtyards still need their own עירוב, even though a שיתוף was made. The רבנן say the שיתוף is enough to cover the courtyards too.

phrases.english: As one Sage holds: one may not rely on it,
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר בן תדאי.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: one may rely on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This explains each side of רב יוסף's statement in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר בן תדאי says we do not rely on it, and the רבנן say we do.

steps.title: רב יוסף's proof from two rulings of רב
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף proves his explanation. רב ruled like רבי מאיר, who says we do not rely on a שיתוף instead of an עירוב. רב also ruled like רבי אליעזר בן תדאי. It seems both rulings come from one reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: How do I know this? Because רב יהודה said in the name of רב that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר. And רב ברונא said in the name of רב that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן תדאי. What is the reason? Is it not because both rulings share one reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings evidence for his explanation by pointing to two rulings that רב gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Later, רבי מאיר holds that we do not rely on a שיתוף in place of an עירוב, and רב ruled like him. רב also ruled like רבי אליעזר בן תדאי. רב יוסף argues that רב ruled like both because both views say the same thing: a שיתוף cannot replace an עירוב. That shows רבי אליעזר בן תדאי's view is really about שיתוף, not about ברירה.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do I say this? (introduces a proof)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain רבי אליעזר בן תדאי. רבה says it is about ברירה, for a barrel bought together. רב יוסף says it is about not relying on a שיתוף instead of an עירוב. רב יוסף proves his view from the fact that רב ruled like both רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר בן תדאי.
steps.whyThisMatters: The proof works only if רב's two rulings share one reason. That kind of reasoning is easy to challenge, and אביי does challenge it in step 11.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: From where do I say this?
As Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר holds we do not rely on a שיתוף in place of an עירוב. His view is explained later.

phrases.english: And Rav Beruna said that Rav said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Eliezer ben Taddai.
What is the reason?
Is it not because it is one and the same reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This brings a proof for רב יוסף's explanation in steps 8 and 9.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that רבי אליעזר בן תדאי's view is about not relying on a שיתוף instead of an עירוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב ruled like both רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר בן תדאי, which suggests the two views share one reason.

steps.title: אביי asks why two rulings were needed
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף. If both of רב's rulings come from one reason, then one ruling should have been enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But if it is one reason, why do I need two rulings?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's proof from Step 10. If both rulings come from the same idea, saying both is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said that רב ruled like רבי מאיר and also like רבי אליעזר בן תדאי because both rulings share one reason: we do not rely on a שיתוף instead of an עירוב. אביי points out that if this were true, רב would only need to say one ruling. We could figure out the other ruling ourselves.

keyTerms.meaning: why do I need it? (it seems extra)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But if it is one reason,
why do I need two rulings?!
phrases.notes: A classic גמרא objection: something looks extra.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי חַד טַעְמָא, תַּרְתֵּי הִילְכְתָא לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that רב's two rulings share one reason
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two rulings come from one reason, one of them is extra. רב would not say something extra.

steps.title: The two rulings teach that we do not combine two stringencies
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the two rulings teach a rule: in עירובין we do not follow two stringencies together.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that we do not act according to two stringencies in the laws of עירובין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's question. The two rulings are not extra, because they teach us a lesson about how to rule in עירובין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ruling of רב is strict on a different detail. He follows רבי אליעזר בן תדאי about a שיתוף made with wine, and רבי מאיר about a שיתוף made with bread. Giving both rulings teaches that in עירובין we do not automatically take on two stringencies, so each stringency needed its own ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: the laws of עירוב (a rabbinic area of law)

steps.confusionAlert: Some read this answer as רב יוסף's reply, while others read it as אביי continuing. Either way, the point is the same: the two rulings are not extra. They teach that we do not take on two stringencies in עירובין.

phrases.english: This teaches us
that we do not act according to two stringencies in the laws of eruvin.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the extra ruling teaches a new principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two rulings from one reason would be extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two rulings teach that in עירובין we do not adopt two stringencies together.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a general rule for ruling in עירובין: we do not stack stringencies.

steps.title: What exactly do רבי מאיר and the רבנן say?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי מאיר was mentioned, the גמרא asks for the source of his opinion and the opinion of the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the opinion of רבי מאיר, and what is the opinion of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks to see the actual source for the dispute it mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the גמרא only said that רבי מאיר holds we do not rely on a שיתוף instead of an עירוב. Now it wants the full text of the dispute, so we can see exactly what each side says.

phrases.english: What is Rabbi Meir's opinion, and what is the Rabbis' opinion?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the mention of רבי מאיר from Step 10 and asks for the source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The text of the dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן

steps.title: What foods are used for an עירוב and for a שיתוף
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says an עירוב for courtyards is made with bread, not wine. A שיתוף for an alleyway can be made with wine or with bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: We make an עירוב for courtyards with bread. If they want to make it with wine, they may not. We make a שיתוף for an alleyway with wine. If they want to make it with bread, they may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer by quoting a ברייתא. This first part sets the basic rules of which food works for each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread works for both an עירוב and a שיתוף. Wine works only for a שיתוף. This difference will matter in Step 16, where the dispute is limited to wine.

keyTerms.meaning: making a שיתוף joining the courtyards of an alleyway

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two straight. An עירוב חצירות joins houses inside a courtyard. A שיתוף מבואות joins courtyards that open into an alleyway.

phrases.english: As it was taught: we make an eiruv for courtyards with bread,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם רָצוּ לְעָרֵב בְּיַיִן — אֵין מְעָרְבִין.
phrases.english: and if they wanted to make the eiruv with wine, they may not.
We make a merging for an alleyway with wine,
and if they wanted to make the merging with bread, they may.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question from Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The background rules: bread works for both, while wine works only for a שיתוף.

steps.title: רבי מאיר requires both; the חכמים say one is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says we make both an עירוב and a שיתוף, so children will not forget what an עירוב is. The חכמים say either one is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: We make an עירוב for the courtyards and also a שיתוף for the alleyway, so that children will not forget the laws of עירוב. Otherwise they will say, 'Our fathers never made an עירוב.' These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: either we make an עירוב or we make a שיתוף.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the actual dispute. This finishes answering the question of Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Legally, a שיתוף can also work for the courtyards. Still, רבי מאיר requires an עירוב too, as an educational step. The חכמים disagree and say one of them is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: so the laws of עירוב are not forgotten
either an עירוב or a שיתוף is enough

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר requires both an עירוב and a שיתוף, for the sake of educating the children. The חכמים say one is enough.

phrases.english: We make an eiruv for the courtyards and a merging for the alleyway

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לְשַׁכֵּחַ תּוֹרַת עֵירוּב מִן הַתִּינוֹקוֹת,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אוֹ מְעָרְבִין אוֹ מִשְׁתַּתְּפִין.
phrases.english: And the Sages say: either we make an eiruv or we make a merging.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and states the dispute itself.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר requires both, for education. The חכמים say one is enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source behind Step 10's claim that רבי מאיר does not let us rely on a שיתוף instead of an עירוב.

steps.title: רבי נחומי and רבה argue where the dispute applies
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחומי and רבה argue about the scope of the dispute. The first opinion says that with bread, everyone agrees one is enough. They only argue about wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחומי and רבה disagree about this. One says: with bread, everyone agrees that one is enough. They argue only about wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion: exactly when do רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue? Only the first opinion is given here. The second opinion comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שיתוף was made with bread, the same food could also count as an עירוב. So everyone agrees nothing more is needed. If the שיתוף was made with wine, which cannot work as an עירוב, רבי מאיר says an עירוב is still needed for the children's sake. The חכמים say it is not needed.
steps.confusionAlert: This is only the first of two opinions. Do not treat it as the final answer. The other opinion of רבי נחומי or רבה comes right on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nachumi and Rabba disagree about this,

steps.mimraCoreRuling: First opinion: with bread, all agree one is enough. The dispute is only about wine.
